ac_coverage.criterion: When a schema's '$schema' names a meta-schema, from the embedded 2020-12 set or supplied through the registry, the validator reads that meta-schema's '$vocabulary' and fixes the set of active vocabularies for that schema resource at load time.

A required ('true') vocabulary the validator does not recognise refuses the schema with exit code 2. The message names both the vocabulary URI and the meta-schema that required it, for example 'meta-schema https://example.com/my-meta requires unknown vocabulary https://example.com/vocab/money'. The library returns the same facts as a distinct exported error type that callers can detect with errors.As.
An optional ('false') vocabulary the validator does not recognise is ignored. The schema loads, and documents are checked normally.

Keywords that belong to a standard vocabulary which the meta-schema does not list are treated as unknown keywords. They have no validation effect and are collected as annotations. For example, under a meta-schema that lists core and applicator but not validation, 'minimum: 5' does not reject 3.
A meta-schema without a '$vocabulary' entry activates all standard 2020-12 vocabularies, so the schema behaves exactly as under the official 2020-12 meta-schema.

The format-assertion vocabulary (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/vocab/format-assertion) is recognised. When it is required, the schema loads without error and the loaded schema records that format assertion was requested, readable through the library. 'format' stays annotation-only in this story.
A meta-schema whose '$vocabulary' omits the core vocabulary, or marks it 'false', refuses the schema with a clear message and exit code 2.

A malformed '$vocabulary' refuses the schema with exit code 2 and a message naming the meta-schema and the bad entry. Malformed means a value that is not a boolean, a key that is not an absolute URI, or '$vocabulary' that is not an object.

An embedded schema resource with its own '$id' and '$schema' uses the vocabulary set of its own meta-schema. The outer resource keeps its own set. Example: the outer schema checks 'minimum' while the inner one, under a meta-schema without validation, does not.

A '$schema' naming another draft's meta-schema, for example 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#', refuses the schema with exit code 2 and a message such as 'unsupported $schema: draft-07; only 2020-12 is supported'. The library returns the same facts as an error.

'$schema', '$vocabulary' and '$comment' are registered core keywords with no validation effect and produce no annotation. A passing basic report for {"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","type":"string"} against "x" contains no '$schema' annotation.

Spec-derived tests, each citing the 2020-12 core section (8.1.2 and 8.1.1), cover required known, required unknown, optional unknown, unlisted standard vocabulary, missing '$vocabulary', missing or optional core, malformed entries, embedded-resource vocabularies, format-assertion recording and draft-07 refusal. They run through both the library and the CLI and check exit codes 0, 1 and 2.

breaking_changes: Basic and detailed reports no longer contain '$schema', '$vocabulary' or '$comment' annotations. Existing tests that expected them would need updating.

Basic and detailed reports no longer contain '$schema', '$vocabulary' or '$comment' annotations. This is declared and intended. Tests that expected them must be updated in the same change, not skipped.
findings: F1 (medium): errors from an externally referenced registry resource that declares its own '$schema' lose their type. They pass through the existing refs.go line 212 wrap, fmt.Errorf("...: %v", err). Examples are UnknownVocabularyError and CoreVocabularyError. The CLI still exits 2, so the check still fails closed, but errors.As cannot see the type, which falls short of AC2's library contract for that path. No test covers a $ref-reached resource with its own vocabulary set.

assumptions.text: The recognised set is hard-coded to exactly the eight standard URIs, as the boundary rules require. It is not derived from the keyword registry, which would widen it.
The error types were defined in the T1 file vocabulary_errors.go, because ParseVocabulary needs them to compile. T2 will add the root-package exports and the unsupported-$schema error.
Quoted '$vocabulary' keys in error messages are cut at 80 bytes.

The compile function for $schema and $vocabulary accepts any value. The meta-schema check already rejects a wrong type, and the vocabulary parser in internal/compile reads $vocabulary directly from the document.
The full suite was not run. I ran only ./internal/keywords/..., the root package and ./cmd/...
internal/compile/metaschema_test.go and cmd/jsonschema/metaschema_cli_test.go updated because they asserted the old draft-07 message (story deliberately changes it); every other assertion is kept.
Only known draft URIs (draft-03..07, 2019-09) get the named message; custom meta-schemas supplied via the registry are not rejected.

Updated tests that asserted the old draft-07 message: testdata/metaschema/schema_keyword.json (operator-granted), the draft-07 case in cmd/jsonschema/metaschema_cli_test.go, and the 'error echoes the declared URI' check in internal/compile/metaschema_test.go, which now exempts the unsupported-draft error. All other assertions are unchanged.
The draft name in the message comes from a fixed regexp match on known json-schema.org URIs, never free-form schema text.
A chain from a custom meta-schema that ends in draft-07 stays ErrMetaChain.
I left out a new test for the draft-07 error through the library, since the existing JSON and CLI cases already cover the message.

The real compile path is resolver.compile in internal/compile/refs.go, reached through CompileReached. internal/compile/compile.go only holds compileAt, which the real path calls just for boolean schemas.
The per-resource keyword loop, including the keywords.Lookup call that the inactive-vocabulary routing has to change, is in refs.go. refs.go is not in this task's scope.

Schema is defined in jsonschema.go and is built in compileChecked. The accessor Schema.FormatAssertionRequested() needs a new field there, filled at Compile. jsonschema.go is not in this task's scope either.
The vocabulary step lives in resolver.compile in refs.go, which the operator approved for this run; compileAt in compile.go is the older path and is unchanged.
jsonschema.go is not edited. The flag is stored on the root Node, not on Schema, so no change was needed there.
A keyword whose vocabulary is not one of the eight standard URIs is always active.

The new tests do not cover the error paths (unknown required vocabulary, malformed '$vocabulary', missing core, draft-07). T1 and T2 cover those at the parser level, and T5 will add library and CLI cases.
The new test file is named vocabulary_apply_test.go so it does not collide with vocabulary_test.go, which T5 owns.

spec_test.go globs testdata/*/*.json and treats every file as a spec-group suite. It already skips testdata/metaschema, so I made it skip testdata/vocabulary too. The new case files have their own shape and runner. No assertion was changed.
I added optional_core.json and no_vocabulary.json under testdata/vocabulary/metaschemas/ because the missing-$vocabulary and optional-core cases need them. Both sit in the allowed metaschemas folder.

The malformed-$vocabulary case checks only that the error names malformed.json, because the meta-schema check of the supplied meta-schema itself reports it first. The MalformedVocabularyError path is covered by the unit tests in internal/compile.
